notes.system: Template-owned. Replaced wholesale by sidecar-update.yml on every upstream release.
notes.system_if_uninitialized: Template-owned only while the file still contains real {{TOKEN}} markers (the rail greps for specific setup tokens like {{ACCOUNT_ID}}, not a blanket '{{' — templates mention {{PLACEHOLDER}} in prose). Once setup fills it, the file is the user's and is never touched again — it is skipped and named in the update PR instead. Only FILL-IN TEMPLATES belong here: a file that is written once and then owned. A file that ACCUMULATES content belongs in system_if_absent — see the note there.
notes.system_if_absent: Delivered ONLY when the file does not exist, and never touched again — the check is existence, not content. JOURNAL.md and DECISIONS.md accumulate: a user appends to them for months. Token-gating them was a data-loss bug (fixed 1.7.1). The gate asks 'does this still contain a placeholder', which for an accumulating file answers 'yes' for as long as any one token in its header goes unfilled — so a journal with two months of real entries and a single {{AUTONOMY}} left in its standing-rules block was replaced wholesale by the 40-line seed, under a PR body promising the journal was untouched. Existence is the only safe test for these.
notes.user: Never touched by tooling. JOURNAL.md, DECISIONS.md and LOOP_PROMPT.md appear here and in a system class; the ownership test resolves the overlap — placeholder tokens for LOOP_PROMPT.md, existence for JOURNAL.md and DECISIONS.md. A repo that predates DECISIONS.md simply doesn't have the file, so the rail delivers the seed on the next update and never touches it again.
notes.workflow: .github/workflows/sidecar-update.yml cannot update itself (GITHUB_TOKEN may not push workflow-file changes). When the rail changes upstream, the update PR body flags it as a one-file manual copy.
